CV-X UM_A 6-97

Control/data output via I/O terminals Using command inputs via I/O terminals I/O command inputs available on the controller

The I/O command inputs available on the controller are shown below. See the descriptions in the following pages for more details on each command.

1: ON (short), 0: OFF (open) Reference

Except for image capture and clear error, the I/O commands can be input only when the controller is operating in run mode.

To confirm a command, input the command to CMD_PARAM0 to 7, CMD_CODE0 to 3 and then turn the CST input on (recognition of the leading edge).

ACK output and NACK output ON time is of the same duration as STO output time.

As the commands based on real-time execution are executed along with the measurement process, execution of that kind of command does not affect the image processing. However, command execution time for this case will take longer than when the command alone is solely executed.

If the switched program is set to [Internal], the time for inputting the trigger after switching the program fluctuates. A delay of one trigger interval may occur.

Do not use with the external master registration input at the same time. The sequence for switching programs and the external master registration process will vary.

The response of the image displayed on the IV Smart Navigator might be delayed until after switching programs (BUSY output OFF).

 Program switch error

If using the program expansion function for the SD card (Page 8-10), a program switch error occurs when the advanced program information cannot be read from the SD card.

For example, bit0 to bit6 input changes and switches to P099 when the SD card is removed.

A program switch error occurs. BUSY output turns OFF and error output turns ON. Run output turns OFF and operation stops. The previous program number will be retained but the device cannot run. Clear error input is disabled. The PWR/ERR indicator light on the sensor amplifier turns ON (red). The sensor head operation indicator light blinks (red).

Connecting the control panel or IV Smart Navigator (IV-H1SN) and clearing the error messages cancels the errors and the device changes to the settings screen. Error output turns off. The program number changes to 'P000'.

For details about how to clear the program switch error, refer to 'How to clear a program switching error' (page 7-4) .

After the process is canceled, the image taken before cancellation is registered as a master image. The master image registration process is delayed by the cancelling process. Delay time depends on the settings.

If the setting for writing to ROM is set to [Disable], only the master images of active programs selected in the settings mode is written to ROM.

An image for external master registration will not be reflected to the backup file (iv4a) of the batch backup/individual program backup performed while running.

If the setting is set to [Enable], do not turn OFF the power during the master registration time (T3). Otherwise, all or part of the setting data may be lost.

The operation will be the same as the one when [Write to ROM when using Ext. Master Save] is set to [Disable] for the programs saved in the ROM in the sensor, regardless of the settings of [Write to ROM when using Ext. Master Save].

AI trigger processing is performed for each image capture to detect trigger ON/OFF. If the result of AI trigger processing is trigger OFF, the judgment processing by the detection tool is not performed.

If the previous trigger is off and the AI trigger process is trigger ON, the AI trigger is output and judgment processing is performed.

After the judgment process is completed, the status output updates and the strobe output is turned ON. Confirm that the strobe output is turned on, and then import the status output.

Images captured during the judgment process are processed by the AI trigger after the judgment process is completed (follow-up processing).

If a trigger on is detected in the follow-up process, AI trigger output and judgment processing for the target image are not performed, and an AI trigger error occurs. An AI trigger error will not be cleared even if the next normal AI trigger is established. Execute the clear error input.

If the judgment process exceeds 1 s, the trigger buffer error output turns on. If trigger buffer error output is turned on, no trigger error will occur even if there is a trigger on in the follow-up process.

Total Status NG | When the total status result is NG, the output turns ON.
RUN | When the sensor is running and no system error has occurred, the output turns ON.
BUSY | The output turns ON in the following cases. • Judgment process in progress (capture process/ image process) • Switching programs • Registering the external master image • Data transferring to an SD card (in the case of settings enabled)
Trigger Ready | Output turns on when the trigger can be accepted.
Strobe | Output turns on when the total status result is refreshed.
Transfer file | Output turns on during the transfer of the result file.
Error | The output turns ON when the following errors occur. • System error • Startup memory readout error • Program switching error • External master registration error • SD card access error The following errors are output when settings are [Enable]. • Trigger Error • FTP error • SD card transfer error • Trigger Input Time Error • Strobe Error • SNTP Sync Error • Tact Warning (when AI Trigger is Enabled) • AI Trigger Output Error (when AI Trigger is Enabled) • AI Trigger Buffer Errors (when AI Trigger is Enabled) • AI Trigger Capture Speed Warning (when AI Trigger is Enabled)
SD card error | The output turns ON when the following errors occur. • SD card access error • SD card transfer error (when settings are [Enable])
Insufficient SD capacity | Output turns on when the SD card does not have sufficient capacity.
AI Trigger Output | One-shot output when the AI trigger turns on. The one-shot output time can be set in [Sensor Advanced] > [I/O Settings] > [Output Settings] > [AI Trigger Output].
Tool 00: Position Adjustment | When the status result of the position adjustment is OK, the output function turns ON.
Tool 01 to 64 | When the status results of the detection tool and position adjustment tool are OK, the output function turns ON. Status results can be output by each tool.
Master 00 to 07 | • When master image settings are enabled and the status results for all tools, except the position adjustment tool, are OK with the selected master image set, the output function turns ON. • If the status result for multiple master numbers is OK, the supported output functions turn ON.
Logic 1 to 8 | When the status result of the specified logic is OK, the output turns ON.

top_results.title: AS_149726_LJ-S8000_UM_L02US_KA_GB_2035_2.pdf
top_results.content:
AS_149726_LJ-S8000_UM_L02US_KA_GB_2035_2.pdf | 5-81

Setting item | Settings
Start Digit | Specifies the position of the detected code at which to start reading data.
Read Data Length | Specify the number of characters (Byte unit) data to read from the start position.
Split Data | When enabled, the read data is partially cut out and output as cut out data. Cut data can be matched with patterns.
Output Fixed Length | When enabled, data is output for the number of characters set in the read data length. If the number of read characters is insufficient, it is completed with the character data specified in "Filling Character (1 byte)".
Call Text at Read Error | If enabled, the character data specified in "Text Called" will be output when reading fails.
Output Symbol Identifier | When enabled, a symbol identifier (3 bytes) defined by the ISO / IEC 15424 / JIS X 0530 data carrier identifier (including the symbology identifier) is added to the beginning of the read data.
Expansion Channel Interpretation (ECI) | When enabled, ECI is output as the result of reading code that contains ECI. It does not affect the read operation of code that does not contain ECI.

Font Color | Compare the text and background colors and set which color should be recognized as a character. • Black: Black portions will be recognized as text. • White: White portions will be recognized as text.

Block Target | If the cut-out is not being performed properly due to background noise, sometimes changing the cut-out target will allow cut-out to be performed.

Controller PROFINET communication specifications Control and data output by PROFINET Controller PROFINET communication specifications Standard specifications

The PROFINET communication of this system supports two types of communication: "data I/O communication (cyclic communication)" and "record data communication (acyclic communication)."

Data I/O communication (cyclic communication)

This is a function to make periodic communication at specified update time intervals and is suitable for real time control.

The update time and communication size depend on the connection settings on the PLC (maximum communication size: 1408 bytes or 1252 bytes when using a communication expansion unit).

See "Typical setting procedure for PROFINET" (Page 6-194) for more details. Record data communication (acyclic communication)

This is a communication method to use dedicated commands to access to a "record" which is a piece of byte information divided in the unit of 1024 bytes.

Two types of commands, Read Record and Write Record, are available. When these commands are executed, a response to the command is returned.

This method can be used for communication which does not require real time processing.

It is possible to access to the addresses exceeding the maximum size allowed for the cyclic communication (1408 bytes; or 1252 bytes when using a communication expansion unit).

Ensure that the writing size is specified in units of 4 bytes.

Each record is assigned with an index. Data is accessed based on the specified index and size.

For the controller's Ethernet port and for communication expansion units, the accessible ranges for each piece of byte information are as follows:

Output data (received by the controller): Read/write

Input data (sent from the controller): Read only

The Read Record and Write Record commands are issued from the PLC by using the "RDREC" (SFB 52) and "WRREC" (SFB 53) blocks respectively. See "Typical setting procedure for PROFINET" (Page 6-194) for more details.

If the Write Record command is issued while the Parameter module is being written in the cyclic communication, memory area conflict may occur. Design the use of the Write Record command to avoid the memory area conflict with the cyclic communication.

Program Setting Protection

To allow the use of a program setting saved in the computer only for a restricted set of VS cameras, set a password and the MAC addresses of the target VS cameras. Add the MAC addresses of the target VS cameras in the list in Manage MAC Addresses.

When you load a program setting to a VS camera whose MAC address is not registered in the MAC Address list, you need to enter the password. If the entered password is correct, the program setting is loaded.

#D039

Settings Protection can only be executed by an account which has the Full Control permission level.

The [Settings Protection] dialog box will appear when you select [Settings] - [Settings Protection] from the menu bar. You can protect the following three types of settings:

Tool Protection: Restrict the editing of tools by setting a password and selecting tools to protect.

Vision Dashboard Protection: Restrict the editing of the Vision Dashboard by setting a password.

Program Setting Protection: Restrict the VS cameras that can use the program setting by setting a password and the MAC addresses of the cameras to allow.

Restrict the editing of tools by setting a password in order to prevent unauthorized modification of tools and leak of technical information. By protecting tools, you can hide them in the task and restrict editing via the context menu. Set one password for the set of tools that you selected. You can change or release it later.

The following information are not displayed for protected tools even if they are selected in the task.

Tool properties in the [Properties] view Setting parameters in the [Data List] view

Operations allowed for protected tools in the task are only grouping and ungrouping. Other operations such as copying are not allowed in the task.

Image Acquisition Capture Simulation Image Capture

The simulation image capture allows you to check of the actual images being captured by the camera based on the changed settings, or save the captured images to the SD card in the image format specified in the output settings. This is useful for quickly checking camera settings and saving images for simulation in XG-X VisionEditor.

Live Image Check this box to display live images through a continuous feed. Point [Live Image] is only applied in Setup Mode.

If the capture on trigger input is disabled in the trigger settings (Page 2-36), this check box is always unchecked and the setting cannot be changed.

When [Live Image] is selected for a moving object, take care when capturing as there will be a time lag between the external trigger input and the actual image capture.

[Live Image] is applied when the capture unit being edited is being executed (waiting for a trigger input). When the image capture buffer is enabled, the images collected in the buffer will still be displayed even if the capture unit is not running, as long as it is waiting for a trigger.

[Live Image] is not available in the case of LumiTrax Mode (Page 7-18), LumiTrax Specular Reflection Mode (Page 7-39), MultiSpectrum Mode (Page 7-56), 3D Capture Mode (Page 776), Outline Capture Mode (Page 7-96), or when HDR capture (Page 2-34) is enabled.

By [Settings] on the menu bar, you can configure the following settings for the program setting. See the explanation of each item for more details.

Total Status Settings: Set the judgment target(s) (tools and/or cell) for the main task.

Execution Error Settings: Set whether to issue an execution error when the value being referenced by the tool is invalid.

Position Adjustment Reference Settings: Create a setting so that, when you add a measurement tool, the position adjustment of a different tool is automatically applied to the measurement tool.

Archive Condition Settings: Set the archiving conditions.

Recording/Simulation Image Settings: Specify the save destination folder for the recorded images, the folder from which the simulation images are loaded, and detailed settings for the loaded images.

Settings Protection: Set to restrict edits to be made for the tools and the Vision Dashboard, and allow only a restricted set of VS cameras to use the program setting.

You also need to enter the password when you turn the Program Setting Protection switch OFF.

Clicking this button opens the [Change Password] dialog. Enter the old password and a new password, and then click [OK].

Manage MAC Addresses

Clicking this button opens the [Enter Password] dialog. Enter the password and click the [OK] button. Then, the [Manage MAC Addresses] dialog opens. Set the target MAC addresses (maximum of 100 MAC addresses).

-Add : Clicking this button opens the [Edit] dialog. Enter a 12-digit MAC address. -Delete : Selecting a MAC address and clicking this button deletes the MAC address.

-Edit : When you double-click a MAC address or click the (edit) icon, the [Edit] dialog appears. Edit the MAC address.

Enter a MAC address of an alphanumeric string of 12 characters without [:] or [-]. In the [Manage MAC Addresses] dialog, the MAC addresses are displayed with [:] or [-] added.

The Program Setting Protection will take effect after rebooting or after changing program settings.

Settings Protection The password uses an alphanumeric string of 4 to 32 characters.

You also need to enter the password when you turn the Vision Dashboard Protection switch OFF.

Clicking this button opens the [Change Password] dialog. Enter the old password and a new password, and then click [OK].

Program Setting Protection

To allow the use of a program setting saved in the computer only for a restricted set of VS cameras, set a password and the MAC addresses of the target VS cameras. Add the MAC addresses of the target VS cameras in the list in Manage MAC Addresses.

When you load a program setting to a VS camera whose MAC address is not registered in the MAC Address list, you need to enter the password. If the entered password is correct, the program setting is loaded.

Setting [Program Setting Protection]

To set Program Setting Protection, turn the switch to ON (default: OFF). When you set the switch ON, the [Set Password] dialog appears. Enter a password and click the [OK] button. Then, the [Password Confirmation] dialog opens. Enter the password again and click the [OK] button.

The password uses an alphanumeric string of 4 to 32 characters.

You also need to enter the password when you turn the Program Setting Protection switch OFF.

Clicking this button opens the [Change Password] dialog. Enter the old password and a new password, and then click [OK].

Manage MAC Addresses

Clicking this button opens the [Enter Password] dialog. Enter the password and click the [OK] button. Then, the [Manage MAC Addresses] dialog opens. Set the target MAC addresses (maximum of 100 MAC addresses).

-Add : Clicking this button opens the [Edit] dialog. Enter a 12-digit MAC address. -Delete : Selecting a MAC address and clicking this button deletes the MAC address.

-Edit : When you double-click a MAC address or click the (edit) icon, the [Edit] dialog appears. Edit the MAC address.

Enter a MAC address of an alphanumeric string of 12 characters without [:] or [-]. In the [Manage MAC Addresses] dialog, the MAC addresses are displayed with [:] or [-] added.

The Program Setting Protection will take effect after rebooting or after changing program settings.

Signal: RUN; Signal Description: Run mode output; Function: This signal is output while the controller operates in run mode.

3. Tool Settings (Standard Mode)

4 Sensor Setup Extended Functions for the Blob Count Tool Select the [Extended Functions] tab and configure the settings.

 Advanced Color Extraction/Advanced Brightness Extraction z For color type Specifies a color to be extracted using HSV (H: Hue, S: Saturation, V: Brightness).

Set the upper limit and lower limit for the range of 0 to 359. Lower limit ≤ Upper limit

The extraction range of a color is from the lower limit to the upper limit.

Lower limit > Upper limit The extraction range of a color is from 0 to the upper limit, and from the lower limit to 359.

S Set the upper limit and lower limit for the range of 0 to 255. The extraction range of a color is from the lower limit to the upper limit. V

You can adjust the value by slider while confirming the color histogram. The values within the range specified by the sliders will be used as the brightness.

The vertical axis indicates the extracted pixel.

Among the pixels of each color to be extracted, the maximum one becomes the maximum value of the vertical axis.

By pressing [LIVE image], the range of the extracted color can be set based on the Live Image of the target.

z For monochrome type

Sets the upper and the lower limit of the brightness to be extracted in a range within 0 to 255.

The extraction range of the brightness is from the lower limit to the upper limit.

Adjust the value by slider while confirming the monochrome histogram.

The values within the range specified by the sliders will be used as the brightness.

The vertical axis indicates the extracted pixel.

Among the extracted pixels of each brightness, the one that has the most pixels becomes the maximum value of vertical axis.

By pressing [LIVE image], the range of brightness to be extracted can be set based on the Live Image of the target.

 Size Limit Setting

Sets the range of a blob size (area) to be counted. Adjust the threshold for the size by checking the matching rate.

The maximum size (area) extracted as a blob in the master image is set as the matching rate of 100. The target is counted when the matching rate is within a threshold range, and "Size NG" when it is outside the range.

Press [LIVE image] as needed, and take an 'OK' image and an 'NG' image. The image which the sensor is currently imaging will be displayed.

If [Trigger Options] is set to [External] or [Internal Trigger Control/AI Trigger Control] is set to [Enable], input an external trigger.

If the external trigger cannot be input, press [Trigger ON] to take an image of the target by temporarily using the internal trigger.

Select [1-200] or [1-999] according to the range of the matching rate necessary for judgment.

 Boundary Exclusion Sets whether to count or exclude the target that protrudes from the window.

Press [LIVE image] as needed, and take an 'OK' image and an 'NG' image. The image which the sensor is currently imaging will be displayed.

z Reset Status Output on Clear Error Execution  Enable

Resets status output when clear error is input. Judgment-related outputs and errors will be turned off until the judgment result by the next trigger input is output.

If a PC, control panel, or display expansion unit is connected, the image used for judgment will be reset and the [Waiting for trigger] screen will appear.

 Disable (default) Does not reset status output when clear error is input. Judgment output cannot be reset with this function via the field network.

To do a reset via the field network, use [Status result/Buffer clear request]. 'Chapter 9 Connecting to a Network' (page 9-1)

7 Various Functions Sensor Advanced Settings z Write to ROM when using Ext. Master Save

Writes data to the ROM of the sensor when master image registration is performed using the external input or field network. 'Registering the Master Image' (page 11-11)

 Disable (default)

Writes only the master images of active programs selected in the settings mode to the ROM of the sensor. The other data will not be written.

The following triggers are subject to control: Standard Mode/Sorting Mode: Internal Trigger, AI Trigger

AI Through Count Mode: Trigger Operation

As input to IN1 is turned on, or the field network cyclic communication trigger request is turned on, the target trigger is issued at intervals determined according to the setting, and the image is captured.

'Trigger Options' (page 4-7)  Disable (default) Does not control the target trigger with input to IN1.

[Internal Trigger Control/AI Trigger Control] is a setting common to all programs. It cannot be set for each program.

Edge Sensitivity | Sets the percentage of waveform peak to be recognized as an edge when the largest change in gradation is 100%. Peaks of waveforms below this edge sensitivity are not recognized as edges, which is useful for ignoring noise.
Edge Filter Width | Edge strength waveform can be averaged. When a noise component causes false edge detections, increasing the filter width can reduce the false detections.
